data.title: SpaceX in Talks to Access 80,000 US Cell Towers for Starlink Mobile: Report
data.description:
SpaceX is in talks with major US tower companies to gain access to as many as 80,000 cell sites for Starlink Mobile, following the company’s FCC approval to acquire Tristar’s AWS-3 spectrum. The towers would give SpaceX a ground network to work alongside its direct-to-cell satellites.

Crown Castle is among the tower owners SpaceX is negotiating with, according to people familiar with the matter who spoke to Bloomberg. American Tower and Vertical Bridge, the other two large tower owners in the US, could also be involved. American Tower declined to comment, while SpaceX and Vertical Bridge did not respond to requests for comment. Any agreements could be worth billions of dollars.

Crown Castle CEO Chris Hillabrant did not name SpaceX during the company’s third-quarter earnings call on Wednesday, but he did not rule it out either. “You can assume that we’re talking to all parties,” said Hillabrant, who also called SpaceX’s recent purchase of low-band spectrum a “huge milestone.”

SpaceX’s goal is to become the fourth national wireless carrier in the US, and Elon Musk outlined the plan on SpaceX’s own earnings call. “We will be building out our terrestrial networks so there’s broad-based connectivity anywhere that SpaceX and Starlink are allowed to operate,” said Musk. He added that satellite launches and spectrum “will pave the way for Starlink Mobile to become a major mobile carrier in the US.”

The FCC has already approved SpaceX to operate 15,000 satellites that connect directly to phones, and Starlink Mobile now has more than 22 million monthly users.

T-Mobile already partners with SpaceX on direct-to-cell service in the US, and has expanded its Starlink satellite roaming to Canada and New Zealand.

data.title: Tesla building Western Canada’s first factory-owned Collision Centre in Port Coquitlam: Scoop
data.description:
Tesla owners in B.C. who end up in a fender bender may soon have a new place to get their cars fixed, straight from the automaker itself.

Tesla has announced it plans to build its own collision repair centre in Port Coquitlam, the same city where it opened a 60,000-square-foot Service and Delivery Center last year.

In a post on LinkedIn, Rishi Bakshi, Tesla’s new BC Collision Manager, said he is leading the launch of what he called “Western Canada’s very first factory-owned and operated Tesla Collision Center.”

According to Bakshi’s LinkedIn profile, he previously spent more than a decade at Boyd Autobody & Glass as its regional development and area manager for B.C., before working as a regional manager for Speedy Glass in B.C.

He added that the company is now putting together the facility’s founding team.

Who Tesla is hiring

According to Bakshi, Tesla is recruiting in Port Coquitlam for collision body technicians at every level from apprentice to journeyperson, along with paint preppers and detailers.

He pointed applicants to open listings on Tesla’s Career’s website and said new hires would get repair training directly from the manufacturer, including work on aluminum and structural components.

Listings include roles for a Collision Technician and an Apprentice Collision Technician.

Why it matters

A factory-run centre would let Tesla handle that work in-house, in a province with one of the highest EV adoption rates in North America.

Some B.C. body shops, such as AutoMind in Coquitlam, already belong to Tesla’s approved collision centre program, and get Tesla training and tooling but are independently owned. On its collision support page, Tesla describes its own collision centres as facilities that handle everything from cosmetic fixes to full structural repairs.

Port Coquitlam would be Tesla’s third factory-owned collision centre in Canada. The first, a dedicated Tesla Collision Center in Oakville, Ontario, opened in 2022, while a second opened in Montreal in 2023.

Tesla hasn’t announced when the new Collision Centre will open or where in Port Coquitlam it will be located.

data.title: Tesla Pulls the Plug on Cybertruck for Australia and New Zealand
data.description:
Tesla has told Australians and New Zealanders holding Cybertruck reservations that the right-hand-drive version of its electric pickup won’t be coming after all.

The email landed in inboxes on Friday morning in both countries, with a number of customers sharing the email on social media.

“After careful consideration, plans to produce Cybertruck for Australia and New Zealand have been discontinued. As a result, we’re unable to fulfill your reservation and it will be cancelled,” Tesla wrote.

Customers were told a separate message with refund details would follow, and that any money they paid would be returned within 30 days. Because both countries drive on the left, the truck would have needed a dedicated right-hand-drive build, and that is the version Tesla has now decided not to make.

As an apology for “any inconvenience caused,” Tesla is offering affected customers 12 months of FSD (Supervised) at no charge, but it only applies to buyers who place an order for a Model 3 or Model Y. With the subscription running AU$149 (C$147) a month in that market, the offer works out to roughly AU$1,788 (C$1,759) for the year, but it does nothing for buyers who had their hearts set on the truck itself.

For many, the email closes out a wait that began when the Cybertruck was unveiled in 2019. Australians put down AU$150 (C$148) to hold a spot, and the warning signs had been there for a while, with Tesla quietly pulling its Australian reservation page back in 2022.

Canadian buyers are in a very different position. The left-hand-drive Cybertruck remains on Tesla’s Canadian site, with the Premium All-Wheel Drive starting at $139,990 and the Cyberbeast at $167,990, both inflated due to the current tariff situation with the U.S.

data.title: Chery considers building vehicles in Canada using idle plants or partners: Report
data.description:
Chery is now looking at building vehicles in Canada, only days after the Chinese automaker shifted its Canadian sales launch to early next year.

Speaking with Bloomberg at the company’s Wuhu, China headquarters, executive vice president Guibing Zhang said Chery is weighing a few options, including using idle capacity at plants that already exist or teaming up with partners.

“Even without the American market, Canada is a market that is worth having a factory for manufacturing,” said Zhang. “We are looking for the suitable opportunity and communicating on the possible formats.”

According to the report, Chery is looking at idle capacity and talking with Canadian investors interested in Chinese carmakers, although Zhang didn’t name any companies.

Zhang also said fellow Chery vice president Charlie Zhang has been talking often with Industry Minister Mélanie Joly, who sat down with Chery, BYD and Geely representatives while visiting China in June.

“If we can find some good ways to merge with partners, not only just from investments from Chery but from different parties, and if we can get the manufacturing going — I think that is something that the Canadian government would welcome,” said Zhang.

If it goes ahead, the report says Chery could become the first Chinese automaker with a manufacturing presence in Canada.

Idle plants have been a recurring topic this year, with BYD, Geely and Chery reportedly considering Ontario’s CAMI plant and Stellantis looking at importing China-built Jeep EVs while its Brampton plant sits idle.

Related Articles:

  • Chery shifts target to early next year for Canadian launch
  • BYD, Geely, and Chery reportedly considering Ontario’s CAMI plant for Canadian production

data.title: 2027 Ford Mustang Mach-E gets standard extended range battery and new Trail package
data.description:
While Ford has decided to kill the F-150 Lightning, they aren’t quite giving up yet on the Mustang Mach-E. The electric SUV is getting more range as standard and a new package aimed at gravel roads and campsites.

The automaker detailed the 2027 Mustang Mach-E on Thursday, a few weeks after its EV sales sank 80% in the third quarter as the Mach-E and Lightning struggled.

Extended range battery for every trim

For the first time, the extended range battery comes standard across the whole lineup, and the smaller pack is gone.

Select and Premium models get 88 kWh of usable capacity, while the GT and Rally carry 91 kWh.

Ford credits a new, cheaper front motor that matches the old unit’s performance. In the U.S., the Select RWD now starts at US$39,995 before destination.

Ford says final EPA range estimates will come closer to availability.

The new Mach-E Trail

The Trail is a factory-built US$2,295 package that can only be added to the Select eAWD.

It raises the ride height by 10 mm up front and 15 mm at the rear compared with the Select and Premium, using specially tuned passive struts and springs.

It also borrows the Rally’s steering rack, 19-inch dark grey wheels and Michelin CrossClimate 2 tires, and adds 400W Pro Power Onboard, with plugs behind the centre console and in the cargo area.

“It’s built for all-season, off-pavement excursions,” said Nick Rallis, Ford’s lead Mach-E vehicle integration engineer, adding that the tires bring “a significant traction benefit in winter conditions as well.”

Visually, it stands apart with a Carbon Black front fascia section and a Trail logo on the centre armrest.

Trail buyers also get 100,000 extra Ford Rewards points beyond the 22,000 given with every Mach-E, which can go toward accessories such as a Thule clamp-on cross bar kit.

What about Canada?

U.S. orders opened on October 22, and the Trail is expected to start arriving in the first quarter of 2027.

Ford.ca already teases the Trail package, but it still lists 2026 trims and hasn’t published Canadian pricing for the 2027 lineup.

data.title: Tesla’s $10.1 billion Project Crystal Sun Wins Key Approval in Texas
data.description:
A Texas county has granted significant tax incentives to Tesla’s proposed solar factory. The board of commissioners unanimously approved the $10.1 billion project.

Tesla has received a bevvy of incentives to build a solar cell manufacturing facility in Fort Bend County, Texas. The plant, codenamed Tesla Project Crystal Sun, will receive tax relief for up to 35 years if the American company builds in the county.

The tax breaks come in four tranches. Tesla will benefit from an abatement that exempts it from or lowers property taxes for a set period. A Chapter 381 agreement may also give Tesla other incentives tied to investment and job creation.

The Foreign Trade Zone (FTZ) Non-Objection with Payments in Lieu of Certain Taxes will reduce Tesla’s customs costs when importing manufacturing equipment or raw materials. Lastly, the Payment in Lieu of Taxes (PILOT) “True Up” agreement allows the county to adjust the payment terms associated with the incentives if necessary.

Four out of five commissioners supported the incentive package. The fifth board member, interim County Judge Daniel Wong, abstained from voting to avoid bias due to an existing business relationship with Tesla.

Meanwhile, by Tesla’s calculation, Fort Bend County and Texas stand to reap nearly $6.5 billion in taxes in 38 years.

Tesla is still considering multiple sites. The company admitted an unnamed rival location outside the Lone Star State is offering a “very compelling package.”

Nevertheless, Fort Bend officials have several reasons to be hopeful. Tesla already has a production plant about an hour’s drive away in Brookshire, where it makes Megapacks (with reports that it was considering adding solar manufacturing). CEO Elon Musk did note that his company is working to integrate all production processes, including the supply chain. Locating a new site nearby in Texas makes sense from a logistics standpoint.

data.title: Rivian buys UK simulation startup Third Dimension AI to speed up self-driving work
data.description:
Rivian is buying its way into better simulation as it pushes toward hands-free driving and robotaxis. The EV maker announced on Thursday that it has acquired Third Dimension AI, just a week after it launched an early access program for Point-to-Point hands-free driving.

Founded in 2024 by Tolga Kart and Piotr Sokolski, Third Dimension has built a platform that converts real-world data into detailed, controllable 3D environments.

That lets engineers rebuild tricky driving scenarios and tweak them at scale, so Rivian’s autonomy models can practise rare edge cases without waiting for them to happen on real roads.

Rivian says bringing the platform in-house will help power its “end-to-end autonomous driving data flywheel,” pairing real-world driving data with virtual scenarios.

What Rivian is getting

According to TechCrunch, the startup has a 15-person team, mostly based in the U.K., and the deal gives Rivian a chance to grow its AI hub in London.

Third Dimension’s leadership and technical staff will move into Rivian’s autonomy research and engineering teams. Neither company disclosed what Rivian paid.

“Simulation is central to how we train and validate our autonomous driving systems,” said James Philbin, Rivian’s SVP of Autonomy & AI.

“Their technology and expertise will strengthen and accelerate autonomy across our consumer and robotaxi roadmaps,” he added.

Kart, who serves as CEO, said joining Rivian lets the team “deploy our simulation technology at scale.”

Why buy Third Dimension

The acquisition comes as Rivian plans to release a version of its autonomous software by the end of this year that can handle an entire trip, from surface streets to highways, much like Tesla’s Full Self-Driving (FSD).

The company is also working toward full autonomy for robotaxi versions of its R2 SUV, which are slated to launch on Uber’s platform in 2028.

Interestingly, Third Dimension’s technology was first built to speed up video game development before its founders turned to autonomous driving. The startup raised $7 million (C$9.8 million) in seed funding before the deal.

data.title: Kia Canada Wants to Be the Country’s First Affordable EV Brand as Chinese EVs Approach
data.description:
Kia Canada wants to own the affordable end of the electric vehicle market before Chinese automakers get a real foothold here, and it’s leaning on the 2027 Kia EV3, which starts under $40,000, to lead the way.

Kia Canada Chief Operating Officer Elias El-Achhab laid out the plan on stage at an auto industry retail forum in Vaughan, Ontario, on October 20.

As Automotive News Canada reported, he said the company is “trying to be the first affordable EV brand in the country.”

That pitch comes as Canada prepares for more Chinese-built EVs under a deal that, according to the forum coverage, allows up to 49,000 of them into the country each year at a 6.1% tariff. Rather than treating that as a threat, El-Achhab described it as more of a bonus, since Kia’s lineup was already affordable before the deal arrived.

He also argued that being a lower-cost brand makes Kia stronger, not more exposed, because its value comes from the technology and features buyers get for the price rather than just the lowest sticker.

Kia’s lineup of affordable EVs now spans three body styles. The EV3 subcompact SUV starts at $36,995, while the EV4 compact sedan starts at $38,995, both under the $40,000 mark. The EV5 compact SUV sits a step above at $43,495. Buyers wanting more performance can also look at the EV4 GT, which starts at $58,595.

According to El-Achhab, the early signs are encouraging. He said orders for the EV3 and EV5 are already backed up, and that dealers threw their support behind the plan at a recent national dealer meeting. He also noted that roughly nine in 10 EV buyers stay with electric when it comes time to replace their vehicle.

For Canadians shopping for an EV, that means more choice in the price range where it matters most. As Chinese imports begin arriving, Kia is betting its combination of pricing, features and an established dealer network will hold up against both new Chinese brands and Tesla.

data.title: Bulgaria breaks ground on 300 MWh Tvarditsa battery park powered by Tesla Megapacks
data.description:
Tesla doesn’t sell cars in Bulgaria yet, but its Megapacks are already breaking ground there.

Bulgaria’s Prime Minister Rumen Radev joined Tesla representatives in Tvarditsa, in the Sliven region, on October 20 for the start of construction on Battery Park Tvarditsa, according to the country’s Ministry of Energy.

The project lands a few months after Tesla registered a local company in Bulgaria, a move seen as a step toward an official market entry.

The site will be a five-hour energy storage system with 300 MWh of capacity, built around Tesla’s Megapack 2XL.

According to the ministry, it calls for 80 battery units along with twenty 4.4 MVA Tesla transformers.

The first of three projects

Tvarditsa is the first of three storage projects that Asarel-Trade and Power Profit plan to build in partnership with Tesla.

Together, the three sites would add more than 2,300 MWh of storage, and they’re part of an investment program worth more than €350 million (C$550 million).

“Whoever succeeds in building the capacity for reliable, sustainable energy storage holds the key to the future,” Radev said at the ceremony, as reported by BTA.

Energy Minister Iva Petrova said Bulgaria has brought more than 6 GW of storage systems online in under a year and a half, which helped keep power flowing at home and to neighbouring countries through the critical summer period.

Tesla talks investment

Interestingly, the ceremony wasn’t the only Tesla meeting of the day.

Afterward, Radev, Petrova and Innovation and Digital Transformation Minister Ivan Vasilev sat down with Tesla representatives to discuss potential investments in Bulgaria, the ministry said.

No details from that meeting were shared, and no date has been given for a Tesla consumer launch in the country.

The Bulgarian project adds to a busy run for Tesla Energy in Europe, where Megapacks are also powering Belgium’s largest battery project.

Tesla also said last week that its Megapacks are almost sold out.

data.title: China wants automakers to file before OTA software updates
data.description:
China wants automakers to check in with regulators before pushing out new software, a change that could affect how often Tesla owners in China see new features.

The Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT) has opened public comments on draft changes to its vehicle market-access rules, two months after Tesla used an over-the-air (OTA) update to recall more than 2.7 million cars in China over driver monitoring.

What the draft would require

According to the MIIT notice, the revisions would set up oversight rules for software upgrades, cloud-based configuration changes and hardware upgrades carried out by automakers on road vehicles.

As Reuters explains, automakers would have to file with authorities before rolling out software updates or other changes to smart cockpit systems.

Hardware upgrades, including new automated-driving sensors and controllers, would also need to be reported ahead of time if they could affect a vehicle’s safety or energy-efficiency performance.

The package also covers external labelling on vehicles, conditional approval for small-batch models and tighter links between automaker monitoring platforms and the national vehicle safety monitoring platform.

What it means for Tesla

Tesla ships frequent OTA updates, with the biggest update of all, FSD on the horizon. Pre-filing would add a step before every update that touches the cockpit or driving software. Any future hardware change, such as a new FSD computer or camera, would also have to be reported first.

Chinese regulators already keep a close eye on Tesla. In August, Tesla was also part of China’s largest vehicle recall ever, covering nearly 3 million of its cars over emergency door releases.

Earlier this year, the MIIT also proposed mandatory physical controls for essential functions starting in 2027.

This isn’t the first time China has tightened OTA rules either. In February 2025, the ministry said autonomous driving-related OTA upgrades would need regulatory approval, aiming to stop automakers from using updates to hide defects.
